record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.context_brief: Constructing graphs with many interlacing values
record.original_question: For subgraph centrality, is there a simple general construction that produces graphs with many interlacing values, meaning many positive parameters β for which a fixed pair of non-cospectral vertices i and j satisfy [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.6. Let i, j be two non-cospectral vertices of a graph G. We say that i and j interlace at β if SC (i, β) = SC (j, β); β is an interlacing value .
A related, more informal problem is the following: is there a simple way to construct graphs with many interlacing values?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A$. For a vertex $i$ of $G$ and a real parameter $\beta>0$, the subgraph centrality of $i$ at $\beta$ is
$$\operatorname{SC}(i,\beta) \;=\; \bigl[e^{\beta A}\bigr]_{ii} \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\beta^k}{k!}\,[A^k]_{ii}.$$
Two vertices $i,j$ of $G$ are called cospectral if there exists a permutation matrix $P$ fixing the spectrum of $A$ and mapping $i$ to $j$; equivalently, $[A^k]_{ii}=[A^k]_{jj}$ for every $k\geq 0$. For non-cospectral vertices $i,j$, a positive real number $\beta$ is called an interlacing value if
$$\operatorname{SC}(i,\beta)=\operatorname{SC}(j,\beta).$$
Provide a simple general construction that produces, for each integer $N\geq 1$, a finite simple graph $G_N$ containing a pair of non-cospectral vertices $i_N,j_N$ such that the set of interlacing values of $(i_N,j_N)$ in $G_N$ has cardinality at least $N$ (i.e., graphs admitting arbitrarily many, or at least many, interlacing values for a fixed pair of non-cospectral vertices).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published construction addressing this informal problem about producing graphs with many interlacing values for subgraph centrality at a fixed pair of non-cospectral vertices. The notion is recent and appears in the context of new results on subgraph centrality; no follow-up resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Construction of cospectral graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Methods for constructing cospectral graphs employ linear algebraic techniques such as Schur complements, interlacing, and coronals.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist for cospectral graphs but not specifically for many interlacing values of subgraph centrality.

status_evidence.title: Subgraph centrality in complex networks
status_evidence.snippet: Subgraph centrality SC(i,β) = [e^{βA}]_{ii} measures participation of a node in closed walks.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the definition of subgraph centrality used in the problem.
